summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and cough, initially concerning for pneumonia. Imaging revealed diffuse pulmonary opacities, but rapid improvement on repeat X-ray indicated pulmonary edema rather than infection. She was found to have culture-negative peritonitis, with elevated peritoneal fluid white blood cells that decreased with antibiotic therapy. A clogged PD catheter required one session of hemodialysis before resuming peritoneal dialysis, which successfully reduced fluid overload. Antibiotics were transitioned to intraperitoneal vancomycin and ceftazidime for completion as an outpatient. Orthostatic hypotension was managed with midodrine and florinef. She improved clinically, with resolution of respiratory symptoms and stabilization of volume status, and was discharged home in stable condition.
